description.narrative: The objective of the Vietnam Road Asset Management Project is to improve the efficiency and sustainability of the road asset management and maintenance practices performed by the country?s Ministry of Transport on national roads. The project consists of the following components: 1) Road Asset Management System (RAMS) development, with a goal towards financing the development and implementation of a comprehensive Road Asset Management System; 2) road asset preservation, aimed at supporting Performance-Based Contracts (PBCs) to demonstrate more efficient maintenance of selected highways, in addition to funding traditional road asset maintenance works; 3) road asset improvement, with an objective of financing improvement of road assets for high priority road sections of the national road network and other related activities, supervision of improvement works and undertaking of environmental and social monitoring; and undertaking technical, internal and financial audits; and 4) institutional strengthening, aimed at supporting targeted activities to develop the capacity of Vietnam?s road agencies to undertake better planning, budgeting, constructing, and monitoring of road assets.

The proposed Project Development Objective (PDO) is to improve the efficiency and sustainability of the national road asset management and maintenance practices performed by the Ministry of Transport on national roads in Vietnam.

title.narrative: Semi-annual Project Monitoring and Evaluation Report will be submitted to the Bank

comment.narrative: <p>Due to the extension of the project until December 31, 2022, the number of semi-annual monitoring and evaluation reports submitted to the Bank was 18 in total.</p>

title.narrative: PBC maintenance implemented under the project

comment.narrative:
<p>A total of 234km is maintained under PBC method in the project. In which:</p>

<p>- The section of National Highway 2 (km163-Km287) with a total length of 124 km has been maintained under PBC method from 2015 to 2020.</p>

<p>- The section of National Highway 6 (Km193-Km303) with a total length of 110 km has been maintained under PBC method from 2016 to 2020.</p>

title.narrative: Annual condition measurement for national road network

comment.narrative: <p>Surveys were completed and the road surface condition of 25,200.89 km of national highways was updated on the system under the management of 4 Sub-Departments of Road Management.</p>

title.narrative: Km of roads improved under the project

comment.narrative:
<ul>
 <li>The total number of km of roads improved in the original project is 59.64 km including: Package CP1: Upgrade of Trang Thua - Cong Neo bridges on NH 38B; Package CP1A: Upgrade of Trang and Cap bridges on NH38B and Go bridges on NH39 has been completed with a total length of about 7km. Package CP14: Upgrade of NH 39 (Km91+000-Km107+522), the Vo Hoi – Diem Dien section, has been completed with a total length of 12.71 km. Package CP13: Upgrade of NH 39 (km42+714-Km64+000), the Trieu Duong - Hung Ha section, and 02 bridges: Nai and Dong Tu: completed with a total length of 19.07 km. Package CP12: Upgrade of National Highway 38, the section Quan Goi - Yen Lenh bridge (km33+960-Km52+600): completed with a total length of 20.86 km.</li>
 <li>The total km of roads upgraded using the project savings is 20.89 km, including the bypass through Son La city, the NH 6 at the section from km289+950 to km308+820 with the length of 19.5 km, and the NH 2 at the section from km284+600 to km285+995 with the length of 1.39km.</li>
 <li>In total,s of December 31, 2022, about 80.53 km of roads were upgraded under the project</li>
 <li>In addition, the NH9 expansion project, the section from Cua Viet port to National Highway 1, with a length of 13.8 km, financed by the savings of the VRAMP project. Due to delayed implementation of land acquisition and resettlement, the scope of work for NH9 was cancelled by project closing. The client have committed to implement this scope with their financing and is expected to be completed in 2024.</li>
</ul>

title.narrative: Roads in good and fair condition as a share of total classified roads

comment.narrative:
<p>Based on the Intermediate results of Component 2 – Road asset maintenance, 168.4 km have been maintained under traditional maintenance contracts, 234 km have been rehabilitated under PBC maintenance contracts, and 80.53 km have been upgraded. The total klometers maintained and upgraded in the project is 482.93 km, thus the proportion of roads in good and fair condition in the total road network due to the project has increased from 70% to 72.72% (calculated by having total kilometers of roads traditionally maintained/rehabilitated/improved under VRAMP /total number of km national roads = 482.93/17,748km=2.72%)). Total kilometers of national road as determined in the baseline data is 17,748 km.</p>
<p><strong>Note from ICR reporting:</strong> With the increase in National roads network from 17,748km to 20,773.00km, the percentage of roads in good and fair condition should be measured based on actual measurement of such roads from among the total length of roads in that network which implies that <strong>= 482.93/20,773km=2.32 thus the proportion of roads in good and fair condition in the total road network due to the project has increased from 70% to 72.32%</strong></p>

title.narrative: Annual audit of Road Maintenance Fund published and available for civil society

comment.narrative: <p>Currently, the Road Maintenance Fund has been dissolved under the decision of the Government. However, according to Government regulations, the funding for road maintenance is audited annually.</p>

title.narrative: Annual and mid-term (3 years) plans for priority and implementation of national road network maintenance and long-term (10 years) maintenance strategy generated by RAMS

comment.narrative: <p>The RAMS system has been verified, handed over and put into use. The Department for Roads of Vietnam has issued regulations on management, operation, <strong>exploitation</strong>, and use of the RAMS system. Further pilot development of maintenance plans for roads, bridges and 32 assets for some roads managed by Sub-Departments of Road Management.</p>

title.narrative: Expansion of PBC program in national road maintenance

comment.narrative: <p>Performance Based Contract (PBC) financed by the project is 234km. Performance-based maintenance has been replicated by the Department for Roads of Vietnam as a method of maintenance for the entire system of national highways.</p>

title.narrative: Improved financing of road maintenance measured by the increased maintenance financing covered by the RMF

comment.narrative:
<p>- The budget allocated to DRVN (according to MOT’s decision on budget allocation) for road maintenance in 2021 was VND 9,972.5 billion, equivalent to about USD 437.2 million (VCB's selling rate on December 1, 2020: VND 22810/USD) ~121.44% of base year demand (USD 360 million).</p>
<p>- The budget allocated to DRVN (according to MOT’s decision on budget allocation) for road maintenance in 2022 was VND 10,521.59 billion, equivalent to about USD 459.06 million (VCB's selling rate on December 31, 2021: VND 22920/USD) ~127.52% of base year demand.</p>
